:::{#exr-wilks-std-gaussian}
#### Standardizing an approximately Gaussian estimate

Suppose $\hthml \dsim \ndist{\param_0, \einf(\param_0)^{-1}}$,
and define $Z \eqdef \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,(\hthml - \param_0)$.
Show that $Z$ is approximately standard Gaussian,
and find the approximate distribution of $Z^2$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-wilks-std-gaussian}

$Z$ is a linear function of $\hthml$,
so it is approximately Gaussian,
with approximate mean and variance:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{Z}
&= \E{\sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,(\hthml - \param_0)}
&& \text{(definition of $Z$)}\\
&= \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,\E{\hthml - \param_0}
&& \text{(factor the constant $\sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,\paren{\E{\hthml} - \E{\param_0}}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,\paren{\E{\hthml} - \param_0}
&& \text{(the expectation of a constant is that constant)}\\
&\approx \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,(\param_0 - \param_0)
&& \text{(approximate mean of $\hthml$)}\\
&= \sqrt{\einf(\param_0)} \cdot 0
&& \text{(subtract)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(multiply by zero)}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Var{Z}
&= \Var{\sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,(\hthml - \param_0)}
&& \text{(definition of $Z$)}\\
&= \einf(\param_0) \Var{\hthml}
&& \text{($\Var{aY + b} = a^2 \Var{Y}$)}\\
&\approx \einf(\param_0) \einf(\param_0)^{-1}
&& \text{(approximate variance of $\hthml$)}\\
&= 1
&& \text{(a number times its inverse is 1)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $Z \dsim \ndist{0, 1}$.
The square of a standard Gaussian variable has a $\chi^2_1$ distribution,
so $Z^2$ has approximately a $\chi^2_1$ distribution.

:::
